prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, opening the field of moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B001 alone as my final position, with the same three names. The case has not changed in kind but it has been sharpened. Six members independently reach the same configuration, including Johansson and Olsson, who moved to it from fourth place and from a first-place ranking of their own field's candidate. I do not count that as evidence, but it does mean the scientific argument has been tested from several directions without anyone finding a defect in the central chain: a quantitative, falsifiable prediction in 2011 (flat bands and a vanishing Dirac velocity at a magic angle), followed in 2018 by the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity at that regime, followed by independent reproduction in several laboratories and extension to twisted multilayers and moire transition-metal dichalcogenides. A theorist can respect this case because the clue was found in nature and not only derived from first principles. The discovery that the citation honours is the existence of tunable flat-band correlated phases, which does not depend on the pairing mechanism. The citation now says 'there' and avoids any claim that the superconductivity is explained, in line with the concern raised by Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations remain real. The pairing mechanism and several correlated states are still debated, the field is moving quickly, and a committee that values a settled interpretation could reasonably wait another cycle. Attribution is imperfect on the experimental side: Cao as first author and the Fatemi, Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani groups cannot be honoured by one experimental name, and earlier twisted-graphene band theory has some claim on the theory side. Finally B007 is the cleaner two-person attribution and I cannot show that it is scientifically weaker; if the committee puts a stable interpretation and attribution cleanliness ahead of field-opening novelty, B007 is a defensible and legitimate outcome and I would not regard it as an error.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock is a finished capability with stable interpretation and multi-laboratory comparison, whereas twisted bilayer graphene has an unsettled interpretation and an attribution split across experimental groups. He also asks whether the criterion is field-opening breadth or enabling measurement capability.
responses.response: My answer to the chair's criterion question is that for this prize the deciding criterion is what changed in our knowledge of physical systems, and I accept that a new measurement capability is a legitimate basis in general. Kroll is right that the clock has a stable interpretation. But I distinguish interpretation of a mechanism from the stability of the discovery. What Kroll counts against B001 is the pairing mechanism, whereas the reproduced result is the phase diagram itself, and that is as robust across groups as a clock comparison is across institutes. On attribution I concede his point that B001 has the harder allocation, and I have not changed my view that three names with an imperfect experimental side is better than a misleading two-name prize. I note that his Hall link to JILA is a matter of disclosure and I see no need for recusal from my side.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the clock first, treats the magic-wavelength lattice as distinct from the 2005 comb prize, and argues that a citation for B001 would rest on contested interpretation while the clock citation is a measured number.
responses.response: Her distinction between the comb as a tool and the magic-wavelength lattice as a new trapping method persuades me, and I withdraw part of my round-1 argument that the clock merely refines an honoured line. The 2005 and 2012 prizes are not a strong objection to B007. What remains between us is the citation wording. I have rewritten mine so that it asserts only the prediction of the flat bands and the discovery of the phases, which are measured facts in the same sense as the clock uncertainty, and makes no statement on the mechanism. With that wording I do not think B001 rests on contested interpretation. The residual difference is that I weigh the opening of a new tunable class of matter somewhat more than she weighs the cleanliness of the two-name credit, and that is a difference of judgment which I do not claim to settle by argument.

responses.point: Olsson argues that the real attribution risk in B001 lies on the theory side, where earlier twisted-graphene band-structure work exists, so the citation must name the continuum-model prediction of magic-angle flat bands and not twisted graphene in general; she treats the other experimental groups as evidence of maturity.
responses.response: I agree and I have changed my citation accordingly: it now names the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, which is the specific quantitative result of the 2011 paper, and avoids a general claim about twisted graphene. I also adopt her framing that the independent confirmations are evidence of maturity and not primarily a credit grievance, which is a better way to put what I called an uncertainty in round 1. I would keep the caveat that Cao's first-author role is a real experimental-credit question, but the group-leader convention that Eriksson describes is defensible, and it is a matter for the Academy's wording and not for the choice of configuration.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from a two-name to a three-name B001 and argues that waiting for a mechanism would be a stricter standard than applied to other discoveries, while he still lists B007 and B008 as alternatives.
responses.response: I welcome his move and I think it settles the theory-side credit, since the 2011 continuum model is a joint paper. I agree that waiting for a mechanism would be stricter than the committee's practice. He has also noted that the pending redefinition of the second is a similar open maturity point for B007. I would not press that, because Kroll is right that the clock case does not depend on the redefinition. I do not follow him to B008 as an alternative, because the Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger credit has four names for a three-name limit and a contested split.

uncertainties: Whether a single experimental name, Jarillo-Herrero, is an acceptable representation of the 2018 discovery, or whether the committee wants a different allocation than the supplied names allow.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism will, in the committee's judgment, count against maturity, which depends on how much stability of interpretation is weighed against a clearly reproduced phenomenon. I rely on colleagues in condensed matter for this judgment.

Whether the committee prefers field-opening novelty (B001) or an enabling invention with cleaner attribution (B007), which I treat as a matter of values and not a fact that further evidence can settle.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I find no specific conflict for B001, B007 or B023 in my documented connections: my PhD supervisor David Gross, my early mentor Hector Rubinstein, my co-author Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theoretical-physics group, none of whom is a credited name. My own work is string theory and cosmology, so for the condensed-matter and atomic cases I am an outsider relying on colleagues. I note the disclosures by Kroll (Hall and JILA, relevant to B007), Johansson (B058) and Olsson (B030) and consider disclosure sufficient for Kroll's link.
